The lattice has 5 rows: y=0, y=0.288679, y=0.577350, y=0.866025, y=1.154701 \u2014 but the last exceeds 1, so only 4 rows fit, giving 3+4+3+4 = 14 points. Remove one to get 13. The minimum triangle on the lattice has area (1/3)\u00b2*sqrt(3)/4 = sqrt(3)/36 \u2248 0.04811. But boundary triangles (non-lattice-adjacent triples) can be smaller. Rows at y = 0, 0.288679, 0.577350, 0.866025. Row 1 (y=0): x = 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1 (4 points). Row 2 (y=0.288679): x = 1/6, 1/2, 5/6 (3 points). Row 3 (y=0.577350): x = 0, 1/3, 2/3, 1 (4 points). Row 4 (y=0.866025): x = 1/6, 1/2, 5/6 (3 points). Total: 4+3+4+3 = 14. Remove (1, 0.577350) to get 13. The minimum lattice triangle area is a\u00b2*sqrt(3)/4 = (1/9)*sqrt(3)/4 = sqrt(3)/36 \u2248 0.04811. But triangles formed by non-adjacent lattice points can be smaller. For example, (0,0), (1/3, 0.577350), (2/3, 0): det = |(1/3)(0) - (2/3)(0.577350)| = 0.3849, area = 0.192. Still large. The smallest non-lattice triangle: (0,0), (1/6, 0.288679), (1/3, 0): det = |(1/6)(0) - (1/3)(0.288679)| = 0.096226, area = 0.048. Same as lattice minimum. Actually, on a triangular lattice, all elementary triangles have the same area, and any triangle formed by lattice points has area that is an integer multiple of this elementary area. So the minimum is exactly sqrt(3)/36 \u2248 0.04811. This is much larger than 0.005.
